claims.claim: Arm remains a foundational compute architecture/IP layer across mobile, edge and data center; current Alpha primary-filing lineage confirms the business remains financially strong and liquid while the causal royalty path still depends on customer silicon adoption and product cycles.

Arm's architecture ecosystem, licensing/royalty model and CSS expansion create a durable compute-design control point, but RISC-V and customer-specific architecture choices remain credible substitutes rather than hypothetical impossibilities.

The structural thesis is scenario-robust but not monopoly-like: asset-light IP economics reduce direct fabrication exposure while customer concentration and architecture substitution remain successor bottlenecks.

falsifiers: Sustained compute-unit growth accompanied by deteriorating Arm royalty economics would weaken bottleneck/pricing-power claims.
Material architecture displacement at major mobile or data-center customers would weaken substitution resilience.
CSS/advanced architecture adoption that fails to translate into durable royalty uplift would weaken the causal expansion thesis.

risks.risk: Customer concentration can transmit strategic changes at a small number of customers into Arm economics.
RISC-V and in-house architecture choices remain credible long-run substitution paths.

unknowns.unknown: Exact customer-level royalty concentration is not quantified in the current Alpha packet.

claims.claim: The strongest present challenge remains concentration/control/valuation rather than an invented accounting defect: current Alpha evidence identifies concentrated SoftBank control and extreme market expectations while primary filings support strong operating performance and liquidity.

The broad AI/cloud/edge thesis does not erase architecture substitution or customer bargaining power; RISC-V and customer in-house choices remain lawful counterfactuals that should cap confidence rather than block present treatment.
No current cited evidence establishes a present accounting-quality failure, liquidity crisis or governance abuse; manufacturing such a defect would violate the red-team contract.

risks.risk: Concentrated SoftBank control reduces minority-holder governance independence.
Extreme valuation embeds extraordinary execution expectations.
Architecture substitution and customer bargaining power can pressure long-run royalty economics.

contradictions.contradiction: Exceptional business quality and ecosystem control coexist with an unusually thin valuation margin of safety.
contradictions.resolution: Keep Earth business-quality evidence separate from market-expectations risk; this is decision-useful tension, not a methodology blocker.

unknowns.unknown: Exact customer-level royalty concentration is not quantified in this packet.
No current evidence proves a present accounting-quality defect or governance abuse.
